columns.name: prompt_set
columns.comment: Which prompt set produced this plan, as '<id>@<version>'. Nullable: plans written before prompts were versioned cannot say, and inventing a value for them would be worse than an honest NULL.

columns.name: supersedes_id
columns.comment: The plan this one replaces, or NULL. Set when a decided plan is amended: the decided record is never rewritten, so a revision becomes a new row pointing back at what it supersedes. Maps to FHIR CarePlan.replaces. Note what this deliberately does NOT do — it does not change the superseded plan's status. That plan WAS approved; superseding it does not un-approve it, and rewriting the field would destroy the fact the immutability exists to preserve. Whether a plan is still in force is derived from the absence of a successor, not stored. Deliberately NOT a foreign key, though it points at this table's own id. It would be the registry's only self-referential FK, which is a cycle for the SQLite->PostgreSQL copier — and that copier breaks cycles by looking for use_alter, which the registry has no way to express. The value is written only from a row just read, and a dangling one degrades to 'no successor', which is what NULL already means. An index, not a constraint.

semantics.purpose: A saved care plan: the header row. The plan's content lives in health_concerns, plan_goals and plan_interventions beneath it.
semantics.use_when: Asked what plan a patient has. A plan only exists here once it was SAVED — a plan still under review lives in a checkpoint and is not in the database at all, so an empty result means 'none saved', not 'none exists'.

columns.status: What a clinician decided: 'user_edited' (written, undecided), 'approved', 'rejected'. Decided once — a plan is never re-decided in place.
columns.supersedes_id: The plan this one replaces, or NULL. Set when a DECIDED plan is amended: the decided row is never edited, so a revision becomes a new row pointing back. IMPORTANT: superseding does NOT change the old plan's status — it really was approved. To find the plan in force, take the newest row that no other row's supersedes_id points at; do not filter on status.
columns.prompt_set: Which prompt wording produced it, as '<id>@<version>'. NULL on plans written before prompts were versioned.
columns.deferred: JSON. Problems triage deliberately set aside, so an absence can be told from an omission.
